author: Parsifal-2045
body:
#### PR description:

The unit test used an empty `FrameworkGraph`, so it could only follow Python-visible `InputTag` parameters.  Hidden C++ `consumes<>` declarations (e.g. `bunchSpacingProducer` consumed by `hltEcalUncalibRecHitL1Seeded` missing in the report from https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/51200#issuecomment-5208675462) were invisible, so the test could pass while `cmsRun` failed at runtime with `ProductNotFound`.

This PR fixes the test behaviour:
- Add `buildFrameworkGraphFromProcess` to `moduleClosure`: it serialises the already-constructed `cms.Process` via `dumpPython`, adds a dummy `EmptySource`, and runs a short `cmsRun` job with the `Tracer` service to collect the framework's full `consumes<>` dependency information.

- The test now uses `parseTracerLog(buildFrameworkGraphFromProcess(...))` instead of `FrameworkGraph()`, so the closure computation follows both Python-visible `InputTags` and framework-level `consumes<>` declarations. This makes the list of missing modules flagged by the test exactly what is needed to get a running configuration.

- The test report now groups missing modules by the heterogeneous module that ultimately requires them, ordered by data-flow dependency within each group.  Module names are on their own (with the 'needed by' info as
a comment) so the list can be copied directly into a `cms.Sequence`.

#### PR validation:

Tested locally with the bot setup from https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/51200#issuecomment-5208675462 the test correctly reports all missing modules and adding those modules to `DST_HeterogeneousReco` correctly fixes the unit test and produces a runnable configuration.
title: Make `testHeterogeneousMenu` catch hidden consumes
